 Jaitun Nisha Vs. Noor Alam

 Noor Alam Vs. Jetun Nisha
 Order

Vide this common order, court will decide both the revision petitions Nos. 409/18 and 512/18 as they arises from the same impugned order dated 14.03.2018 passed by the court of Ms. Ankita Lal,
Ld. MM, South East, Saket Courts, New Delhi.
2.

The revision no. 409/18 is preferred by accused persons to set aside/quash the charge framed against them for the offence u/s 506 Part-II IPC and appeal No. 512/18 is preferred by complainant Noor Alam for framing the charges u/s. 415/420/385/387/506 and 511 r/w. 120B IPC against the accused persons.
3. For the sake of convenience, both parties will be referred by the same nomenclature by which they were addressed before the Ld. Trial court.
4. The brief facts leading to filing of the present revision petitions are that complainant Noor Alam got married to accused no.1 Jaitun Nisha as per Muslim rites and rituals on 20.04.2008.
Accused no.2 & 3 are parents, Accused no. 4 is brother-in-law, Accused no.5 is sister and Accused no. 6 & 7 are brothers of accused no.1 respectively.

It was represented to the complainant and his parents by the accused side that accused no.1 is B.Ed and her education was the main consideration for the complainant to marry her as he wanted educated wife but later on it was revealed that accused is only B.A and she has not done B.Ed.
It was also revealed that accused no.1 belongs to Main Puri (U.P) but they represented that they have house in Jaitpur.

Accused no.3 had huge liabilities of loans and on 04.06.2008, all accused persons came to the complainant's house and asked for money to repay their huge debt to which complainant didn't agree and said that his own income was meager but accused persons started pressurizing them and suggested him to get separated from his parents and seek partition of his share in property for arranging the money to which complainant refused on which accused no. 4 threatened the complainant.

Accused no.1 went to her matrimonial home with other accused persons on the pretext of meetings her relatives but later on, when complainant tried to contact accused no. 1, he was not allowed to talk to her.

Later on, accused Noor Alam vs Jetun Nisha on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20442806/
1 persons started threatening him to implicate him in false dowry case.

Complainant filed the complaint on 08.06.2008 in PS Jamia Nagar but no action was taken and finally on 05.10.2008 the complainant communicated Talaq to accused no. 1 according to Muslim Laws which was served on 07.10.2010.

On the next day 08.10.2008 complainant received two threatening calls from unknown number including a call from accused no. 4 to 7.
5.

On 09.11.08 accused no. 7 alongwith one person namely Naushad Guddu came to common relative of complainant and the complainant was called there and accused no.7 with his friends threatened to kill him and demanded Rs.2,50,000/- from him.
The false case under 125 CrPC was filed against complainant in UP concealing the factum of divorce and that a civil suit of declaration had been filed in the civil court by the complainant.

On 02.06.09 the accused no. 2 and 3 came to the house of Mr. Munna i.e., neighbour of the complainant to meet the complainant, from there they came to complainant's house where father of the accused no.1 apologized and requested the complainant to re-marry accused no.1 as per Shariat Law to which the complainant flatly refused.

Accused no.3 on 13.06.2009 threatened to kill the complainant on mobile no. (9953634488) and finally on 26.06.2009 complainant received a call from CAW cell Sri Niwas Puri as a complaint was lodged against the complainant by accused persons.

On 28.06.09 the complainant again received the call threatening the complainant to come to CAW Cell to take back his wife or arrange 3 lacs to settle the matter and they threatened to kill him and throw his body in ganda nala.

6. After leading pre-summoning evidence, accused persons were summoned for offence u/s. 506 IPC vide order dated 06.05.2010 and after that complainant examined himself as CW-1 and Shamsuddin as CW-2 in his precharge evidence.
After considering the pre-charge evidence, Ld. MM framed the charge for offence u/s. 506 IPC against all the accused persons vide impugned order dated 14.03.2018.
the impugned order dated 14.03.2018 is assailed by both the parties by filing respective revision petitions.
Grounds of revision taken by the complainant.

7. Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate the contents of complaint, pre- summoning evidence,
pre-charge evidence led by the complainant and material placed on record which prima facie discloses the commission of offence u/s. 415/420/385/387/ 506/511 read with Sec.120-B IPC and prayed to frame the above-mentioned charges against the accused persons.
Grounds of revision taken by the accused persons 8.
Ld Trial Court has taken cognizance for the offence u/s. 506 (II) IPC without going into the merits of the case and without proper appreciation of pre and post charge evidence.
There is no specific allegations against any particular accused.
The complainant had ample opportunity to call police at 100 number but he did not do so and after 5 days lodged a false complaint in PS Jamia Nagar.
The statement of CW-2 is quite contradictory to CW-1 / complainant as complainant nowhere stated in his complaint that on 04.06.2008 he called CW-2 / Shamsuddin.
Therefore, prayed that impugned order be set aside and they be discharged.

10. Perusal of the Trial Court record shows that accused persons were only summoned for the offence u/s. 506 IPC vide order dated 06.05.2010 and same was challenged by the accused before Ld. Sessions Court but order dated 06.05.2010 was upheld vide order dated 07.08.2012.

No doubt court is not bound down to frame charge only for the offences under sections which accused had been summoned; in pre-charge evidence if some other facts have been brought on record then court can always frame charge for different offences than the one for which accused person was summoned.
Perusal of pre-charge evidence of CW-1 and CW-2 shows that nothing new was brought on record and complainant reiterated his testimony what he has stated in his complaint and pre-summoning evidence.

From the perusal of pre-charge evidence ingredients of Sec.415/420/385 IPC are missing and mere bald allegations by complainant without being supported by any other documentary or oral evidence cannot formed basis of framing of charge for grave offences like offences u/s. 415/420/385 IPC.
Therefore, the revision petition no. 512/18 filed by the complainant is liable to be dismissed.
11. Coming to the revision petition No. 409/18 filed by the accused persons wherein they have challenged the framing of charge u/s. 506 IPC against them.

12. It has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Mohammad Wajid & Anr. Vs State of U.P.
& Ors. 2023 INSC 683 as under:-
"SECTIONS 503, 504 AND 506 OF THE IPC 23. Chapter XXII of the IPC relates to Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance.
Section 503 reads thus:-
"Section 503. Criminal intimidation.

entities.text:
Mohammad Wajid & Anr. Vs State of U.P.
& Ors. 2023 INSC 683
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: --Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do any act which that person is legally entitled to do, as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat, commits criminal intimidation.
Explanation.--A threat to injure the reputation of any deceased person in whom the person threatened is interested, is within this section.

Illustration A, for the purpose of inducing B to resist from prosecuting a civil suit,
threatens to burn B's house.
A is guilty of criminal intimidation."

Section 504 reads thus :-
"Section 504. Intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace.--Whoever intentionally insults, and thereby gives provocation to any person, intending or Noor Alam vs Jetun Nisha on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20442806/
3 knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause him to break the public peace,
or to commit any other offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both."

entities.text: Noor Alam vs Jetun Nisha on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Section 506 reads thus:-
"Section 506. Punishment for criminal intimidation. --Whoever commits, the offence of criminal intimidation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both;
If threat be to cause death or grievous hurt, etc.--And if the threat be to cause death or grievous hurt, or to cause the destruction of any property by fire, or to cause an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or to impute unchastity to a woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both."
24.

2) The threat must be with intent;
(i) to cause alarm to that person; or (ii) to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat; or (iii) to cause that person to omit to do any act which that person is legally entitled to do as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat.
27. A bare perusal of Section 506 of the IPC makes it clear that a part of it relates to criminal intimidation.
Before an offence of criminal intimidation is made out, it must be established that the accused had an intention to cause alarm to the complainant."

13. Coming to the instant case, the allegations on the basis of which Section 506 IPC is sought to be invoked against the accused persons are that they threatened to implicate complainant in false dowry cases and they also threatened to kill him if he does not give Rs.2.5 lacs to clear their loan and they also threatened him to kill him if he does not remarry accused no.1.

In Manik Taneja Vs. State of Karnataka, reported in (2015) 7 SCC 423, Hon'ble Apex Court after noticing Section 506, which defines the criminal intimidation observed as under:
"11. ****** A reading of the definition of "criminal intimidation" would indicate that there must be an act of threatening to another person, of causing an injury to the person, reputation, or property of the person threatened, or to the person in whom the threatened person is interested and the threat must be with the intent to cause alarm to the person threatened or it must be to do any act which he is not legally bound to do or omit to do an act which he is legally entitled to do."

entities.text: Manik Taneja Vs. State of Karnataka, reported in (2015) 7 SCC 423
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. In the instant case, the allegation is that the appellants have abused the complainant and obstructed the second respondent from discharging his public duties and spoiled the integrity of the second respondent.
It is the intention of the accused that has to be considered in deciding as to whether what he has stated comes within the meaning of "criminal intimidation".
The threat must be with intention to cause alarm to the complainant to cause that person to do or omit to do any work.
Mere expression of any words without any intention to cause alarm would not be sufficient to bring in the application of this section.
But material has to be placed on record to show that the intention is to cause alarm to the complainant.

From the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that there was no intention on the part of the appellants to cause alarm in the mind of the second respondent causing obstruction in discharge of his duty.

As far as the comments posted on Facebook are concerned, it appears that it is a public forum meant for helping the public and the act of the appellants posting a comment on Facebook may not attract ingredients of criminal intimidation in Section 503 IPC."

15. It is a settled law that for an offence of criminal intimidation, it is necessary to prove that the accused had threatened a person with any injury to his person, reputation or property and while giving the threat, he had the intention to cause alarm in order to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat or to cause that person to omit to do any act which that person is legally entitled to do as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat.

16. In "Mohammad Wajid V. State of UP", 2023 SCC Online SC 951, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has observed that :
"Para 34. ............. We say so because once the complainant decides to proceed against the accused with an ulterior motive for wreaking personal vengeance, etc., then he would ensure that the FIR / complaint is very well drafted with all the necessary pleadings.

entities.text: Mohammad Wajid V. State of UP", 2023 SCC Online SC 951
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The complainant would ensure that the averments made in the FIR /
complaint are such that they disclose the necessary ingredients to constitute the alleged offence.

Therefore, it will not be just enough for the Court to look into the averments made in the FIR / complaint alone for the purpose of ascertaining whether the necessary ingredients to constitute the alleged offence are disclosed or not.

In frivolous or vexatious proceedings, the Court owes a duty to look into many other attending circumstances merging from the record of the case over and above the Noor Alam vs Jetun Nisha on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20442806/
5 averments and, if need be, with due care and circumspection try to read in between the lines.................."

sentences.text: 17. During cross-examination of complainant as CW-1 it has come on record that he is a practicing advocate and he had divorced the accused no.1 on 05.10.2008 and undergone second marriage on 13.12.2009. FIR u/s. 498A IPC has been registered against him and case u/s. 125 Cr.PC was also filed against him in whose execution proceedings u/s. 82/83 Cr.PC are going agianst him in Mainpuri, UP.

The above facts shows that there is matrimonial dispute between the complainant and accused side and accused side has taken legal recourse and got FIR registered against complainant and have also taken maintenance order in favour of accused no.1.

The threats mentioned in the complaint that were allegedly extended by the accused persons were not of such a nature that would cause alarm to the complainant as despite threats and filing of cases he has divorced accused no.1 and got married second time with someone else.
18. None of the alleged threats contained any intent to cause any injury to the person or property of the complainant.
Most of the alleged threats are utterances by the accused persons due to the matrimonial dispute.
It is not specified as to how the alleged threats caused any alarm to the complainant and moved him to do something which he was not legally bound to do.

Merely saying that the accused persons will kill him without there being any further act of legal omission or illegal commission from the side of the complainant will not be sufficient to prima facie constitute the offence under Section 506 IPC.
19.

A plain reading of the allegations does not satisfy the ingredients of Section 506 IPC because an offence of criminal intimidation can be made out only if it is established that the accused persons had an intention to cause an alarm to the complainant.
Mere threats given by the accused persons not with an intention to cause alarm to the complainant would not constitute an offence of criminal intimidation.

20. In view of the above observation, the impugned order dated 14.03.2018 passed by the Ld. Trial Court is set aside and the revision petition No. CR 409/2018 titled as "Jaitun Nisha & Ors. Vs. Noor Alam" is allowed and all the accused persons are discharged and revision petition No. CR 512/2018 titled as "Noor Alam Vs. Jaitun Nisha" is dismissed.
